item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've been stewing on this article ever since it came out, trying to decide if i like it or not. I am now pretty sure that this means I owe it an upvote, one way or another. It's now been over two years since this was first written, and it's certainly not common for an article to be that memorable.

As for my specific thoughts on it,

+ show
- hide

On one hand, I absolutely adore indulgent industrial imagery of this sort. The Pietrykau-Fontaine Array and its AI-driven configuration system are great fun to imagine, and I love the buildup of the way the site is constructed over the borehole. When the borehole is first introduced, my mind immediately jumps to the sorts of things that are called "boreholes" in the real world, usually quite narrow shafts that extend a great distance into the earth. We know it has to be big enough to swallow a huge amount of waste heat, though, so I'm imagining something maybe a meter or so across, big enough to be scary. Then we establish that the entire containment chamber has to be able to drop into the borehole during the FORTY DAYS protocol. Ah, okay, so it's a bit bigger than that, probably tens of meters across. Then we establish that the whole site has to be able to drop into the borehole too. oh. Now my mind is suddenly reeling at the realization that the site's basement level is not, as you would normally expect, excavated out of the underlying soil; it's suspended over an immense, kilometers-deep pit of darkness. With a nuke at the bottom.
Whoa.

This is unbelievably good writing. I'm a big fan.

But then we get to the actual anomaly.

I confess that, as was mentioned to another critic further up-thread, I have not read the entirety of the "How It Ends" series ("2 edgy 4 me" is my excuse, for the time being), so I can only attack this article from the context it gives me directly. I don't think this is entirely unfair; it's been stated many times that SCP object articles on this wiki are expected to stand on their own.

In this article, I see:
- The Foundation Tried to Contain So Hard that it Made a New Anomaly, a trope which has already been played straight at least once previously and seems a little lackluster
- A mysterious and very clichéd laboratory accident that is both embarrassingly incompetent and technologically unrealistic (I have some background in physics, and that's not really how particle accelerator power supplies work, but I understand I'm probably excessively harsh on physics-related articles in general)
- A guy what got magic super powers because of his involvement in the accident, and is now a spooky gravity ghost
- A melodramatic endgame scenario in which all the universes end
- SURPRISE, he has more sinister motives than we were expecting!!!!

I don't really know what to think. This feels like looking at a very well-constructed building whose foundation is resting on sand. I think this article does work out alright overall thanks to the skill with which it was constructed and its overall mood (which is great), but I also think it blew past me a little bit on its edginess factor and big-scary-earth-shattering-emergency stuff. I ultimately find myself wishing I had just a little bit more suspension of disbelief left to work with by the end, something that would let me feel this one a little more.

It's also possible that I'm just too jaded to really appreciate this, and that my expectations are too poorly-formed and unrealistic to be justified, but since the same sentiment seems to be present in this thread before me, I thought I'd try to hash out what I'm feeling. I really want to like this article, and I do, to an extent, but the core concept stops just a little bit short of capturing my imagination.

item.content:encoded:
So… A critical error occurs in testing of Foundation's humongous science project and creates an omnipotent sapient entity, because the project didn't have any safety measures, backup systems or means to work in dangerous areas exept from chief researcher's manual labor whatsoever.

Said entity starts doomsaying and prophesying the End Of The Multiverse. It also offers to solve all problems by Thanos snapping all other Universes out of existense with a classic condition of "just shut down that one and only thing that restricts me in this world".

After a brief discussion O5 Council concludes that these doomsayings may be true and therefore decides to go on and free the omnipotent Multiverse-collapsing entity because "the man that is probably, at least partially inhabiting this omnipotent sentient black hole was really nice guy".

What. Could. Possibly. Go. Wrong? And that is basically the whole ending part.

So what do we have as a result? A black humanoid with godmode on instead of the anomaly, created by a chain of events that require huge ammounts of utter incompetence of Foundation personnel or a direct divine intervention to work. A b-movie plot twist "oh no, who would've thought, that releasing this thing would be bad". And, as a cherry on top, the "this is the only real 001, guys, seriously" part at the start.

No. Just… No.

No vote from me because I've got problems with it but I like the core concept and it's well written.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, I didn't like this one.

The entire premise hinges on the idea of the majority of the O5 council deciding to trust a super powerful being just because O5-1 happened to know him in his past self and because they feel like they don't have any other options at that very second (even though the event they want to avoid is decades away). Needless to say, this feels very uncharacteristic for an organization that has proven time and time again that it treats these anomalies very seriously (and sometimes even excessively). Then, out of nowhere, they decide to trust the promise of a single anonaly even though they have decades on them to figure out an alternative solution. Hell, if they really felt like it, they could keep it contained until 2065 and then use it as a last case scenario in case all else fails.

Well, no, the O5s break character and, whoopdeedoo, 001 breaks free, causes damage, and says some spooky stuff.

Not only is it totally uncharacteristic of the Foundation, but the ending almost feels like a generic scene out of a movie when the monster breaks free and kills those that freed it.

The idea itself isn't particularly interesting, but that's a matter of taste; the really inexcusable bit for me is just the fact that this is an SCP (a 001, for that matter) that only derives its "scare factor" from the idea of the O5s getting stupid.

-1 from me.

item.content:encoded:
Nah, no offense. I'm just taking the piss.

Collapsible so no forum hawking upper-level staff members will get angry about a long post
hide

1) You're right - physics experiment turned into a humanoid demigod is definitely a Dr. Manhattan retread; I'm just tired of hearing about it. Yes, everyone has read Watchmen. I'm aware of the similarities. This has nothing to do with you specifically, just a general exhaustion about seeing the same thing over and over again.

The point I'd argue, though, is that Dr. Manhattan is probably capable of more in general than the Darkbody is. Darkbody is really only good at one thing specifically. As for the psychological maladjustments, there's not really anything that I can say about his characterization before other articles come out.

2) For the sake of convenience, this is posted on the 001 page. I didn't realize this was something anyone would get hung up on - I didn't think it was too much of a stretch to ask people to imagine them accessing this from a different in-universe database. I still don't, so this crit seems super pedantic.

3) There were a lot of things being held at Area-11 (which is mentioned in the second addendum), so they had task forces around for that purpose. After the Darkbody showed up, they sent everyone home.

5) I actually don't think "using a nuclear device to destabilize a singularity" is that much of a stretch. Considering how little they know about the Darkbody, I don't think it's unfair to think that they wouldn't just use the same "containment breach = nuclear bomb" that shows up so many other times in this fiction.

6/7) You know what I meant. You need to understand though that, from an in-universe point of view, this was written by Overseers for each other, as documentation of this thing they discovered. There is obviously subtext that will be left out, which we'll elaborate on (at length, I'm sure). If that doesn't satisfy the mindset of "each article exists only in isolation" (which I personally thing is sort of naive and remarkably stifling from a creative standpoint) then there's not much I'm going to be able to do about that.

Look at it this way. If you saw someone you know acting in a way that seemed remarkably out of character, you'd wonder why he was acting that way, right? You wouldn't just say "ah fuck that guy for acting strange" and then go about your business. By the same token, if you read about a group of individuals acting in direct opposition to nearly everything they stand for, wouldn't you be interested in knowing whether or not there's something else going on instead of directly jumping to "welp, they're acting like morons."

You're certainly free to think about it however you'd like, but I'd ask for the benefit of the doubt. I wasn't going to spam the wiki with every contest page I've got ready (or those of the rest of my teammates!) so yes, the context is delayed. I don't think I've done anything that would make people think I wouldn't deliver, though.

item.content:encoded:
You seem to have taken some offense at my offhand tone, where no offense was meant.
It bears repeating that I enjoyed reading this. My list is just an attempt to be fair and explain why I downvoted despite it being well written.

1)Do you not think the criticism is valid? Seems like a beat for beat retread of Dr. Manhattan's origin story to me. Scientist gets caught in physics experiment, is seemingly destroyed, comes back some time later with ability to control fundamental physics. A case could be made that even their psychological maladjustments run parallel.

2) Don't presume. I would have upvoted if this was not on the 001 hub. Then it would have been a tale in a 001-like format and not subject to my (perhaps unreasonable) high standards for "actual" 001s

3) Fair rebuttal. Honestly did not occur to me that they were guards against break-ins and not -outs. But that begs the question of why the facility needed guards then and not now.

5) The O5 council shouldn't be silly. They have had enough physicists look at this to tell them that it is a singularity, those same physicists would also tell them that blowing it up is less than useless. Contingency plans are great, and more importantly in-character for the council. But not if they don't actually address the contingency in question.

6/7) I read the whole story, it ends with a memo from O5-3.
I get that this is part of your contest entry collection, but every article stands alone.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1) As others have noted, Dr. Manhattan.
2) "…will exist separately from decoy SCP-001 archive.." yet here it is on the list
3) What were the 4 ATFs supposed to do in an emergency? Shoot at the black hole?
4) "The addition of three additional…reactors…" was approved by the Department of Redundancy Department.
5) Dropping a river, a mountain, and nukes on it will not even theoretically disrupt a singularity in any way. All 40 Days would accomplish is irrevocably destroying the one device that has a chance of reestablishing containment after a breach. It is a bad emergency procedure and the overseers should feel bad.
6) He is essentially a gravity elemental (which is hella cool now that I read the phrase). There is nothing about that or the origin story that would imply access to other realities. We only have his word that he can destroy outside this continuity, and the breach shows he is a liar. This means he definitely qualifies as an end-of-the-world/universe threat, but not your new end-of-ALL-worlds threat.
7) "Guys! We should totally let the talking black hole off its leash so it can destroy infinite realities, but not ours. C'mon! Cal's a cool guy." I can't believe that 8/13 of the people with full access to Foundation records are dumb enough to expect that to end any other way than how it did.

I enjoyed reading, but taken together this is too many flaws for an 001. Downvote.
